names.english: Disorders of the Female Genital Tract

ahara: Pungent, sour, salty, alkaline things (paittika type)
Excessive intake of all rasas (sannipatika type)
vihara: Lying in faulty postures after eating

roopa: Vatika: piercing pain, stiffness, crawling sensation of ants, hardness and numbness of vagina, exhaustion; menstrual discharge with sound, painful, frothy, thin, rough
Paittika: burning sensation, inflammation, fever, heat; menstrual flow blue, yellow or black, excessive hot discharge with cadaverous smell
Kaphaja: slimy, cold, itching vagina with mild pain; pale and slimy menstrual flow
Sannipatika: burning sensation and pain; white and slimy discharge
bheda: Sasrja (pitta affecting blood overflows even after conception)
Arajaska (amenorrhea with leanness and abnormal complexion)
Acarana (itching due to organisms, frequent desire for man)
Aticarana (swelling, numbness, pain due to excessive coitus)
Prakcarana (pain in back, waist, thighs, groins from premature coitus)
Upapluta (pale fluid with piercing pain or white mucus; vata+kapha)
Paripluta (swollen, tender, painful tract; menstrual flow blue and yellow; vata+pitta)
Udavartini (menstrual blood takes upward course, discharged with difficulty)
Putraghni (vayu destroys foetus repeatedly due to roughness in sonita)
Antarmukhi (curved vaginal opening with vatika distress in bones and muscles)
Sucimukhi (minute vaginal opening from genetic defect)
Suskayoni (dryness of vaginal opening, painful retention of faeces and urine)
Vamini (semen comes out after 6-7 days with or without pain)
Sandhi (aversion to males, devoid of breasts from genetic defect — incurable)
Mahayoni (dilated, unclosed, painful tract with rough and frothy discharge)
diseases.sadhyata: Mixed — most types curable; Sandhi and Sannipatika with discharge resembling ghee/marrow are incurable

ahara: Excessive rough, bitter, astringent, salty, sour and hot food
Cold, rough, little, mixed, incompatible and uncooked food

roopa: Frothy semen (vata)
Thin semen (vata)
Rough semen (vata), ejaculated with difficulty and little quantity, no fertilization potency
Bluish or yellow, hot, foetid semen with burning sensation during ejaculation (pitta)
Exceedingly slimy semen (kapha)
Semen with blood (due to excessive coitus or injury)
Knotted and precipitant semen with difficulty in ejaculation (suppression of urges)
Semen combined with other dhatus (8th type)

ahara: Cold, rough, little, mixed, incompatible and uncooked food
Excessively sour, salty, alkaline, incompatible and unsuitable food
Regular use of curd, milk and meat of marshy animals
vihara: Wounds in penis from sharp instrument, teeth on nails, wooden stick
Excessive use of awny insects to elongate organ
Faulty application of five evacuative measures
agantuja: Deficiency of rasa and other dhatus

roopa: Looseness of penis
Profuse perspiration and panting during coitus
Fruitless determination and effort
Depressed penis without semen
Pallor
Too weak with low vitality
Little erection
Cardiac disorder, anaemia, bronchial asthma, jaundice, exhaustion, vomiting, diarrhoea, colic, cough, fever (in loss-of-seed type)
Swelling, pain, redness in penis; acute boils; inflammation; ulcers; ring-like hardness; fever; thirst; giddiness; fainting; vomiting (in loss-of-penile-strength type)
bheda: Dhvajabhanga (due to loss of penile strength)
Incurable type (due to genetic defect + sannipata drying up semen-carrying vessels)
diseases.sadhyata: Most types curable; incurable when caused by genetic defect and sannipata drying semen vessels

ahara: Excessively salty, sour, heavy, pungent, burning and fatty food
Fatty meat of domestic and aquatic animals

roopa: Vatika: frothy, thin, rough, blackish or reddish menstrual flow, painful; intense pain in waist, groin, cardiac region, sides, back, pelvis
Paittika: bluish, yellow, very hot, black or deep red, frequent and painful flow; burning sensation, redness, thirst, mental confusion, fever, giddiness
Kaphaja: slimy, pale, heavy, unctuous, cold, viscous flow with mild pain; associated with vomiting, anorexia, nausea, dyspnoea, cough
Sannipatika: symptoms of all three doshas combined
Incurable sign: discharge resembling ghee, marrow and muscle-fat with anaemia, weakness, thirst, burning and fever
diseases.sadhyata: Vatika, Paittika, Kaphaja curable; Sannipatika with ghee/marrow-like discharge is incurable

ahara: Regular intake of salty, sour, pungent, alkaline and decomposed food
Meat of domestic, marshy and aquatic animals

roopa: Vatika: abnormal taste, excessive froth, roughness in milk; child grows slowly, suffers feebleness of voice, retention of stool, urine, wind, vatika head disorder or coryza
Paittika: abnormal colour (blue, yellow, black), foul smell; child suffers abnormal complexion, perspiration, thirst, diarrhoea, constant fever, anaemia, jaundice

Kaphaja: too unctuous milk, slimy milk, heavy milk; child suffers vomiting, tenesmus, salivation, dyspnoea, cough, excessive discharge, feeling of darkness, face and eye swelling, dullness, heart disease
diseases.sadhyata: Curable with purification treatment of wet-nurse
